text:
Sam: seeing a spike in internal DNS timeouts from gpu-pool -> model-backend in us-east-1, started ~10:12 UTC. ~8-12% of requests get `i/o timeout` from the node-local resolver, kube-probe is marking a few replicas Unready. anyone else seeing this?

Jia: yep, seeing similar on our side. can you paste a `dig` and the node-local dns logs?

Sam: here are quick reproductions from one affected node: 
```
$ dig @127.0.0.1 model-backend.namespace.svc.cluster.local +time=2 +tries=2
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 1
;; WARNING: recursion requested but not available
;; SERVER: 127.0.0.1#53(127.0.0.1)
;; WHEN: Tue Mar 18 10:13:01 UTC 2025
;; MSG SIZE  rcvd: 56

# repeated output shows intermittent no answer and then timeout
$ kubectl -n gpu get pods -o wide | grep model-backend
model-backend-57f8d  1/1  Running  0  3m  10.0.2.45  gpu-node-3
model-backend-7c9a2  0/1  CrashLoopBackOff  4  2m  10.0.2.46  gpu-node-7
```

Sam: node-local-dns logs show a lot of UDP retransmit errors and "short read" errors around the same time.

ops-bot: kernel-update-job/east-us-gpu-pool rolled out kernel v5.15.94 -> v5.15.102 on nodes: gpu-node-3,gpu-node-7 at 10:08 UTC :warning:

Mike: interesting — our infra team saw kernel rollout on the same pool. recent kernels changed behavior for reverse path filtering on some NIC drivers. rp_filter can drop UDP packets when asymmetric routing happens, which would look exactly like sporadic DNS UDP timeouts.

Priya: could also be conntrack exhaustion on egress nodes given large number of short-lived flows from model clients. have we got nf_conntrack usage graphs for those nodes?

Nate: quick checks: conntrack shows ~55k entries, limit is 64k on those hosts. Not saturated but climbing. MTU/fragmentation is clean (we didn't see FRAG logs).

Jia: what's the plan? quick mitigation ideas: 1) disable strict rp_filter on affected nodes, 2) force node-local to prefer TCP fallback for upstream queries, 3) roll back kernel if needed.

Mike: agree. we should test disabling rp_filter (sysctl net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter=0) on one impacted node and watch DNS failure rate. if that helps, roll out via daemonset patch. Also consider bumping nf_conntrack_max to 200k as a safety valve.

Sam: doing a canary now on gpu-node-7: `sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter=0`

Sam: after change (2 mins) — application error rate dropped from ~9% to ~1.2% on that node. node-local logs show fewer UDP short reads. :thumbsup:

Priya: nice. let's propagate change to the rest of the pool and follow up with kernel vendor. open runbook PR for node-local config to add TCP fallback and an explicit note about rp_filter.

Nate: I'll also patch cluster-ops to raise conntrack on gpu pools and add an alert to watch DNS short-read rate.

Jia: filing incident doc and linking runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dns-resolver-latency

Sam: thanks all — keeping this thread updated as we roll out.
